mainTopic: רב and שמואל on a קטנה who grew up, the נרש story, and a new משנה on freeing a צרה when the widows are minors or deaf
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a dispute between רב and שמואל about a girl married as a קטנה who grew up, after which another man married her. The גמרא explains that the case is one where the first husband lived with her after she grew up. שמואל still holds the marriage is only rabbinic, because כל הבועל על דעת קידושין הראשונים הוא בועל. The גמרא asks why רב and שמואל argue about this again, since they already disagree about קידושין made on a condition. It answers צריכא: each case was needed. Then a story from נרש seems to show that רב's students did not require the husband to live with her. רב פפא answers that in נרש living together came before the bridal chair. רב אשי answers instead that the רבנן cancelled the snatcher's קידושין, and the ruling follows רבי אליעזר. A new משנה teaches when יבום or חליצה with one widow frees her צרה, depending on whether the wives are minors, deaf, or fully competent. The גמרא asks how a deaf woman can do חליצה at all. רבא distinguishes a woman deaf from the start from one who became deaf later, and אביי begins an objection to רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Did the first husband live with her after she grew up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the dispute is about a case where the first husband had no relations with her after she grew up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not talking about a case where he did not have relations with her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reading of the dispute between רב and שמואל. Maybe it is talking about a case where the first husband never lived with her after she became an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If that reading is correct, רב would hold something big. Growing up alone, with no new act by the husband, would turn the rabbinic marriage into a full one. The גמרא is testing whether רב's view really goes that far.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not?' A way of suggesting how to read a case
He had marital relations

phrases.english: What, is it not where he did not have relations with her?
phrases.notes: "He" is the first husband, after the girl grew up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by asking what exact case the dispute of רב and שמואל (cited just before) is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב's ruling apply even when the first husband had no relations with her after she grew up?

steps.title: No, he did live with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion and says the case is where he did have relations with her after she grew up.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is where he did have relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The case is where the first husband did live with her after she grew up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes away the big claim from step 1. It is not that growing up alone completes the marriage. רב's view rests on the fact that the husband lived with her as an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Rejects the suggestion just made

phrases.english: No, it is where he did have relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading suggested in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of the case. It does not reject רב's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing forces us to say the case had no relations after she grew up. It can be a case where he did have relations.

steps.title: Then why does שמואל disagree?
steps.stepSummary: If the husband lived with her as an adult, it seems the marriage should be complete, so שמואל's view becomes hard to understand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had relations with her, what is שמואל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The new reading creates a problem for שמואל. If the first husband lived with her as an adult, why would שמואל say the second man's קידושין work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living with a woman as an adult can itself be a way of making a full marriage (קידושי ביאה). So once he had relations, the first marriage should seem complete, and nobody else should be able to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: If
What is the reason?

phrases.english: If it is where he had relations with her,
what is the reason of שמואל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's view based on the case defined in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the second man's קידושין take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Relations after she became an adult should create a full marriage, so the second man's קידושין should not work.

steps.title: His relations rely on the original קידושין
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that a husband who lives with his wife means to rely on their first קידושין, not to make a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that anyone who has relations does so based on the first קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. The husband did not mean his relations to be a new act of marriage. He was just living with her under their old קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her old קידושין were only rabbinic, because she was a קטנה. Since his relations lean on those old קידושין, the marriage stays rabbinic, and the second man's קידושין can still take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
Anyone who has marital relations
With the intention of relying on the first קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule: כל הבועל על דעת קידושין הראשונים הוא בועל. A husband's relations rely on the original קידושין and are not a new act of marriage.

phrases.english: He holds: anyone who has relations

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת קִדּוּשִׁין הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הוּא בּוֹעֵל.
phrases.english: has relations with the intention of the first קידושין.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כׇּל הַבּוֹעֵל עַל דַּעַת קִדּוּשִׁין הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הוּא בּוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of the one challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Relations after she grew up would be a new, full act of marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: The relations rely on the old rabbinic קידושין, so the marriage stays rabbinic.

steps.title: They already argued about this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב and שמואל already argue about this same idea in another case: קידושין on a condition, followed by marrying her without mentioning the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once. It was said: if he made קידושין on a condition and married her without saying anything, רב says she needs a גט from him, and שמואל says she does not need a גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: why record a second argument between רב and שמואל when they already disagree about this exact idea somewhere else? It now quotes that other argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other case, a man made קידושין on a condition, and then married her without mentioning the condition. If the condition was not met, רב says she needs a גט, and שמואל says she does not. The question is whether the relations rely on the old קידושין, so the two disputes look like repeats.

keyTerms.meaning: But they already argued about this once
As it was stated (an אמוראים teaching)
A condition
He married her without saying anything (about the condition)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא, דְּאִיתְּמַר:
phrases.english: But they already disagreed about this once, as it was stated:
He made קידושין with her on a condition, and married her without saying anything,
phrases.notes: The case assumes the condition was not actually fulfilled.

phrases.english: רב says: she needs a גט from him,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט.
phrases.english: and שמואל says: she does not need a גט from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason given in step 4 to show that the two disputes overlap.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to record the dispute of רב and שמואל about the קטנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same principle is already disputed in the case of a condition, so the second dispute seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Laying out the reasons to show it is the same argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each side of the condition case, showing that שמואל's reason is word-for-word the same rule as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says she needs a גט because once he married her, he gave up his condition. שמואל says she does not need a גט, because anyone who has relations does so based on the first קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasons in the condition case to finish its challenge. It shows that שמואל uses the very same rule here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reasons that marrying her means he gave up the condition, so the marriage stands. שמואל reasons that the relations rely on the first קידושין, condition included. Since the condition failed, there is no marriage. Because the reasoning matches the קטנה case, the dispute looks repeated.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he married her
He fully gave up his condition

phrases.english: רב says she needs a גט from him,
because since he married her, he gave up his condition.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט,
phrases.english: And שמואל says she does not need a גט from him:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַבּוֹעֵל, עַל דַּעַת קִדּוּשִׁין הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הוּא בּוֹעֵל!
phrases.english: anyone who has relations does so with the intention of the first קידושין!
phrases.notes: This is the same rule from step 4, so the challenge is that it's one argument stated twice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט כֵּיוָן דְּנַסְבַהּ אַחוֹלֵי אַחֲלֵיהּ לִתְנָאֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 5 by giving the reasons behind each side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for two separate disputes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's reason in the condition case is the same rule used in the קטנה case, so the two disputes overlap completely.

steps.title: Both disputes were needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers צריכא: from each case alone, we could have thought that one side would agree to the other in the other case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. If only the condition case had been said, we would say רב rules that way only there: because there was a condition, once he had relations he gave it up. But here, in the קטנה case, he might agree with שמואל. And if only this case had been said, we would say שמואל rules that way only here, but in the condition case he might agree with רב. So both were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that each dispute teaches something new. Each side might have agreed to the other in the other case, so both cases had to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason in the condition case is that the husband gave up a condition. In the קטנה case there is no condition to give up, so we might have thought רב agrees the relations rely on the old קידושין. Likewise, we might have thought שמואל uses his rule only for the קטנה case, and agrees with רב where a condition exists. Now we know each holds his view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to state both cases)
I might say / one might think
He agrees with him
In this one / in that one

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא answers the question 'why say it twice?' Each case could have been limited by its own special reason, so both were needed to show that רב and שמואל keep their views in both cases.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב actually agrees with שמואל in the קטנה case, or that שמואל agrees with רב in the condition case. The 'אֵימָא' lines only describe what we might have thought without both statements.

phrases.english: It was necessary, for if only that one had been said,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the condition case from step 5.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָהִיא קָאָמַר רַב, מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא תְּנָאָה,
phrases.english: in that one רב rules this way, because there is a condition,
and since he had relations, he gave up his condition.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָא, אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ, לִשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: But in this one, I might say he agrees with שמואל.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the case of the girl married as a קטנה who grew up.

phrases.english: And if only this one had been said:
in this one שמואל rules this way,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ, אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַב,
phrases.english: but in that one, I might say he agrees with רב,
so it was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 5–6 that the dispute was repeated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב might agree with שמואל when there is no condition to give up, and שמואל might agree with רב when there is a condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both disputes are needed to show that each אמורא keeps his view in both cases.

steps.title: The Neresh story seems to contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רב requires the husband to live with her after she grows up, using a story where רב's students let the first marriage stand without that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say that only if he lived with her as an adult the marriage holds, and if not, it does not? But in נרש a girl was betrothed as a minor, grew up, and was seated on the bridal chair. Then another man snatched her away. רב's students were there, and they did not require a גט from the second man!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks how we understood רב's view. It brings a real story where the first husband had not yet lived with her, yet רב's students still treated her as his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב's reason was that living with her as an adult creates a full marriage. In נרש the husband only seated her on the bridal chair, with no relations mentioned. Since רב's own students did not require a גט from the snatcher, it looks like no adult relations were needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He lived with her as husband and wife (had relations)
A real incident, a story that happened
The bridal chair used at the wedding
Snatched her away
A גט, a bill of divorce

phrases.english: And did רב really say
that when he lived with her, yes,
phrases.notes: He means: when the husband lived with her after she grew up, the marriage is complete.

phrases.english: and if he did not live with her, no?
But there was that incident that happened in נרש,
where she was betrothed while she was a minor,
and she grew up, and he seated her on the bridal chair,
and another man came and snatched her from him.
And רב ברונא and רב חננאל,
the students of רב, were there,
and they did not require her to get a גט from the second man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling why both cases are needed (צריכא), the גמרא now questions the exact condition in רב's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב requires the husband to live with her as an adult for the marriage to be complete.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's students ruled that the first marriage held even though the husband had only seated her on the bridal chair, with no relations.

steps.title: In נרש they live together before the bridal chair
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that in נרש the custom was to live with the bride first and only afterward seat her on the bridal chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In נרש they first marry and live with her, and only afterward seat her on the bridal chair.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. In that town, being seated on the bridal chair meant the husband had already lived with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only looked like a problem because we assumed no relations had happened. Because of the local custom, the husband had already lived with her as an adult, so this fits רב's condition perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: They marry first, meaning they live together first
And afterward

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
In נרש they first marry,
phrases.notes: Here 'marry' means the husband actually lives with her.

phrases.english: and afterward they seat her on the bridal chair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּנַרֶשׁ מִינְסַב נָסְיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the נרש story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts of the case (local custom)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the husband in נרש had not lived with her as an adult.
steps.terutzMaskana: In נרש living together comes before the bridal chair, so the condition of רב was met.

steps.title: The רבנן cancelled the snatcher's קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the snatcher behaved wrongly, so the רבנן cancelled his קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He acted wrongly, so they acted toward him in an unusual way. The רבנן cancelled his קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second answer to the נרש question. Even if the first husband never lived with her, the second man's קידושין did not count because the רבנן cancelled it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer was about the first husband. רב אשי looks at the second man instead: as a penalty for snatching, the רבנן removed his קידושין. That is why no גט was needed from him, and the story proves nothing against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Not properly, wrongly
They cancelled, uprooted
The Sages

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
He acted improperly,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man who snatched her.

phrases.english: therefore they treated him in an unusual way,
and the רבנן cancelled his קידושין.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הוּא עָשָׂה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהוֹגֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic penalty cancels the second marriage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No גט from the second man means the first marriage was complete.
steps.terutzMaskana: No גט was needed because the רבנן cancelled the snatcher's קידושין, not because the first marriage was complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of הפקעת קידושין, the power of the רבנן to cancel a marriage, which comes up in other places in ש״ס.

steps.title: What if he was מקדש with relations?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: cancelling works if the קידושין was with money, but what if it was done through relations?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: That works if he was מקדש with money. If he was מקדש through relations, what happens?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's answer. He sets up the question of how the רבנן can cancel קידושין that was done through an actual act of relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, the רבנן can declare the money ownerless, so there was never a valid קידושין. But with relations there is no object to take away; the act really happened. So how can it be undone?

keyTerms.meaning: That works well, that is fine
Money
Relations, one of the ways of making קידושין

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:
That works if he was מקדש with money,
if he was מקדש through relations, what then?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תִּינַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the רבנן cancelled the snatcher's קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cancelling is easy with money, but an act of relations cannot simply be erased.

steps.title: The רבנן made his act זנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן declared his relations to be זנות, not an act of קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן made his act of relations into an act of זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא. The רבנן cancel קידושין through relations by declaring that the act counts only as זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act did happen, but the רבנן take away its legal meaning as קידושין. So no marriage was made, and no גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it, they declared it to be
An act of relations outside marriage, with no קידושין

phrases.english: The רבנן made his act of relations an act of זנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An act of relations cannot be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן declared the act to be זנות, so it never made קידושין.
steps.whatToRemember: The נרש story has two answers. רב פפא says the husband had already lived with her. רב אשי says the רבנן cancelled the snatcher's קידושין, even when done through relations, by calling it זנות.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל (quoted by רב יהודה) and also רבי אלעזר rule that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. And רבי אלעזר also said: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion of the earlier משנה by giving the final ruling. Two separate אמוראים rule like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the argument in the earlier משנה about the minor girl. Two different אמוראים agree, so the ruling is like רבי אליעזר, and the minor is taught to do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling
And likewise, and so too

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
And likewise רבי אלעזר said:
The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב and שמואל discussion and gives the final ruling on the earlier משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, as both שמואל and רבי אלעזר rule.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר and רבי אליעזר look almost the same, but they are two different people. רבי אלעזר is giving the ruling, and רבי אליעזר is the one he rules like.

steps.title: New משנה: two minor orphans, two deaf wives, or one of each
steps.stepSummary: If a man married to two minor orphans or two deaf women dies, יבום or חליצה with one frees the other. But if one is a minor and one is deaf, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man was married to two orphan girls who were minors, and he died, יבום or חליצה with one of them frees her צרה. The same is true of two deaf women. But if one is a minor and one is deaf, יבום with one does not free her צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches when יבום or חליצה with one wife frees the other wife (her צרה) from the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two minors have the same kind of marriage, and so do two deaf women, so one can free the other. A minor and a deaf woman are each married only מדרבנן, but in different ways, so one cannot free the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Orphan girls who are minors (married off by mother or brothers)
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום
Frees, exempts
Her co-wife
Deaf women (who also cannot speak)

phrases.english: משנה:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי לִשְׁתֵּי יְתוֹמוֹת קְטַנּוֹת, וּמֵת —
phrases.english: One who was married to two orphan minor girls, and he died —

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָתָהּ אוֹ חֲלִיצָתָהּ שֶׁל אַחַת מֵהֶם
phrases.english: יבום or חליצה with one of them
frees her co-wife.
And the same is true of two deaf women.
A minor and a deaf woman —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ.
phrases.english: יבום with one of them does not free her co-wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי לִשְׁתֵּי יְתוֹמוֹת קְטַנּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the final ruling on the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both wives have the same kind of marriage (two minors or two deaf women), יבום or חליצה with one frees the other. A minor and a deaf woman cannot free each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that a wife can only free her צרה when both have the same kind of marriage.

steps.title: Mixed pairs: the stronger wife's release frees the weaker one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. With a פקחת and a חרשת, יבום with the פקחת frees the חרשת, but not the reverse. The same is true for a גדולה and a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one widow is a hearing woman and one is deaf, his relations with the hearing one free the deaf one, but relations with the deaf one do not free the hearing one. If one is an adult and one a minor, relations with the adult free the minor, but relations with the minor do not free the adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases where a man left two wives and his brother does יבום with one of them. Here the two wives are not equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 both wives were the same kind, so either one could free the other. Here one wife has a stronger marriage (the פקחת or the גדולה) than the other (the חרשת or the קטנה). The stronger bond can free the weaker one, but the weaker bond cannot free the stronger one.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who can hear and speak, fully legally competent
A deaf-mute woman
Relations; here, doing יבום by living with the widow
Frees, releases (the other wife from the יבום bond)
An adult woman / a minor girl

steps.whatToRemember: One-way rule: the stronger wife's יבום frees the weaker one, but the weaker wife's יבום does not free the stronger one.

phrases.english: A competent woman and a deaf-mute woman:
phrases.notes: These are the two widows of the same man who died.

phrases.english: relations with the competent one free the deaf-mute,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בִּיאַת הַחֵרֶשֶׁת פּוֹטֶרֶת אֶת הַפִּקַּחַת.
phrases.english: but relations with the deaf-mute do not free the competent one.
An adult and a minor:
relations with the adult free the minor,
but relations with the minor do not free the adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּקַּחַת וְחֵרֶשֶׁת — בִּיאַת הַפִּקַּחַת פּוֹטֶרֶת הַחֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 14, moving from two equal wives to two unequal wives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wives are unequal, יבום with the stronger one frees the weaker, but not the reverse.

steps.title: Can a deaf woman even do חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It said חליצה with one חרשת frees the other, but another משנה says a חרשת's חליצה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a deaf-mute woman able to do חליצה? We learned in a משנה: if a deaf man does חליצה, or a deaf woman does חליצה, or a woman does חליצה with a minor boy, her חליצה is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and raises a contradiction. Our משנה assumed a deaf woman can do חליצה, but another משנה says she cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the משנה said that with two deaf wives, יבום or חליצה with one frees the other. That only works if a חרשת's חליצה counts. The other משנה lists a deaf woman's חליצה as invalid, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone able to do חליצה
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a contradicting source)
Invalid, does not work
A minor boy

phrases.english: GEMARA
Is a deaf-mute woman able to do חליצה?
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה in step 14, which said חליצה with one of two deaf wives frees the other.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
a deaf man who did חליצה, and a deaf woman who did חליצה,
and a woman who does חליצה with a minor boy:
her חליצה is invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's assumption (step 14) that a deaf woman can do חליצה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that חליצה with one deaf wife frees the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה rules a deaf woman's חליצה invalid, so how can our משנה count it?

steps.title: רב: the משנה means relations, not חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: our משנה is only talking about ביאה, not חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: the משנה is talking about relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the contradiction by limiting our משנה to יבום through relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the freeing in our משנה only happens through ביאה, the משנה never claims that a deaf woman's חליצה works. That removes the clash with the other משנה, which only rules her חליצה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to relations (יבום), not to חליצה

phrases.english: רב גידל said in the name of רב:
It is referring to relations.
phrases.notes: He means: when our משנה says one deaf wife frees the other, it only means through יבום, not through חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: אַבִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say a deaf woman's חליצה frees her co-wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only יבום by relations is meant, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבא: deaf from the start versus deaf later
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה can mean חליצה too. Our משנה is about a woman who was deaf from the start, and the other משנה is about a woman who was hearing and later became deaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you can even say it refers to חליצה. Here it is a woman who was deaf from the beginning; there it is a woman who was hearing and then became deaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps חליצה in our משנה and splits the two sources into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of limiting our משנה to ביאה like רב, רבא says each משנה is talking about a different deaf woman. A woman deaf from the time she married can do חליצה. A woman who became deaf after marrying cannot. Step 19 explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces a different answer that keeps the original reading)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)
From the beginning
She became deaf

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say a deaf woman's חליצה is always fine. It only works if she was already deaf when she married.

phrases.english: רבא said:
You can even say it refers to חליצה.
Here it is a woman who was deaf from the beginning,
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה, where the חליצה works. "From the beginning" means she was already deaf when she first married.

phrases.english: and there it is a woman who was competent and afterward became deaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 16, different from רב's answer in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to talk about the same deaf woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is a woman deaf from the start, whose חליצה works. The other משנה is a woman who became deaf later, whose חליצה is invalid.

steps.title: Why being deaf from the start makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reason: a woman deaf from the start leaves the bond the same way she entered it. A woman who married while hearing must say the חליצה words, and she can no longer speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman deaf from the beginning leaves the same way she entered. A woman who was competent and then became deaf cannot, because the reading holds her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבא's split between the two kinds of deaf women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman deaf from the start was married in a weaker way, so a weaker חליצה without speaking is enough to release her. A woman who married while hearing had a full marriage, so her חליצה needs everything, including saying the required words. Since she can no longer speak, her חליצה cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as one enters, so one leaves (the release matches the strength of the marriage)
Holds back, is required (without it the act does not work)
The reading, the words the יבמה must say at חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the strength of the release matches the strength of the marriage. A woman deaf from the start can do חליצה. A woman who married while hearing and then became deaf cannot, because she can't say the required words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea of the sugya: a deaf woman's marriage and release are weaker than a hearing woman's. That also explains the one-way rule in the משנה (step 15).

phrases.english: A woman deaf from the beginning:
just as she entered, so she leaves.
phrases.notes: Her marriage was done without full speech and understanding, so a release without the spoken words is enough for her too.

phrases.english: A competent woman who afterward became deaf: no,
because the reading holds her back.
phrases.notes: At חליצה the יבמה must say set words aloud. Without them it doesn't work, and she can no longer say them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֵרֶשֶׁת מֵעִיקָּרָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּעָל — הָכִי נָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבא's answer in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the split between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It might seem that all deaf women should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The release matches the marriage. A woman who married while hearing needs the spoken reading, which she can no longer say.

steps.title: אביי questions whether a woman deaf from the start can do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks רבא's distinction by quoting a משנה. When the deaf brother dies, the hearing brother may only do יבום with the deaf widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Is a woman who was deaf from the start really fit for חליצה? Doesn't a משנה teach: two brothers, one hearing and one deaf, are married to two unrelated women, one hearing and one deaf. If the deaf man, husband of the deaf woman, dies, what does the hearing man, husband of the hearing woman, do? He does יבום. If he later wants to divorce her, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer from Step 18. He brings a משנה where a deaf widow is given only יבום as an option, not חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a חרשת מעיקרא can do חליצה. In this משנה, the deaf widow falls to her hearing brother-in-law, and the only option listed is כונס (יבום). That suggests a deaf woman cannot do חליצה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
From the start, here meaning deaf already when she married
Fit to do חליצה
Unrelated women, not sisters of each other
He takes her in, meaning he does יבום
A hearing, fully competent man or woman

steps.confusionAlert: Here נׇכְרִיּוֹת does not mean non-Jewish women. It means the two wives are not related to each other.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who just said a woman deaf from the start can do חליצה.

phrases.english: And is a woman deaf from the start fit for chalitza?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one hearing and one deaf,
are married to two unrelated women,
one hearing and one deaf.
If the deaf man, husband of the deaf woman, died,
what should the hearing man, husband of the hearing woman, do?
He takes her in through yibum.
And if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from Steps 18-19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a חרשת מעיקרא can do חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה gives a deaf widow only the option of יבום, which implies she cannot do חליצה.

steps.title: The quoted משנה continues with the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: If the hearing brother dies, the deaf brother does יבום with the hearing widow and can never divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the hearing man, husband of the hearing woman, died, what does the deaf man, husband of the deaf woman, do? He does יבום, and he can never divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with the opposite case. This only completes the source; אביי's real point comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the deaf brother is the יבם. He can marry the widow through יבום, but he can never divorce her. This half is not the part אביי needs. The key case is the one before it, where the widow is deaf.

keyTerms.meaning: He may never divorce her
A deaf man, treated in this context as not legally competent

phrases.english: If the hearing man, husband of the hearing woman, died,
what should the deaf man, husband of the deaf woman, do?
He takes her in through yibum,
and he may never divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה begun in Step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deaf יבם may do יבום with his hearing sister-in-law but may never divorce her.

steps.title: אביי argues the משנה is about a woman deaf from the start
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the deaf widow in the first case was deaf from the start. Since the משנה only allows יבום, she cannot do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the משנה talking about a woman who was deaf from the start? And it teaches: יבום, yes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws his proof from the משנה. The widow there was presumably deaf from the start, and she is only allowed יבום. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מאי לאו suggests the plain reading: the deaf woman was deaf when she married. The משנה says יבום "yes," which hints that חליצה is "no." That would directly contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it so that...? It introduces a proposed reading used as proof.
It teaches
Yes

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from the FIRST case (the deaf husband died), where the widow herself is deaf. It does not come from the second case.

phrases.english: Isn't it talking about a woman deaf from the start?
And it teaches: yibum, yes,
phrases.notes: The thought goes on: יבום yes, but by implication חליצה no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in Steps 20-21
steps.raayaObject: That a חרשת מעיקרא cannot do חליצה, against רבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two brothers, where the deaf widow is given only כונס (יבום)
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 18) that a חרשת מעיקרא can do חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The deaf widow in the quoted משנה was presumably deaf from the start, and the משנה allows only כונס (יבום). This implies she cannot do חליצה, which contradicts רבא.
